story: CFS was formed in 2018 as a spin-off from MIT's Plasma Science and Fusion Center. Its goal was to use new high-temperature superconductor (YBCO) magnets to build a far smaller, higher-field tokamak. MIT and CFS agreed to jointly design and build SPARC, a compact tokamak meant to show net energy. Eni put in $50M at launch.
product: High-field tokamak fusion systems based on HTS magnets: the SPARC demonstrator and the ARC commercial power plant.
wedge: HTS (YBCO) magnet development with MIT, the first roughly three-year phase of the SPARC programme.
became: The best-funded fusion company, building SPARC in Massachusetts and planning ARC in Virginia, with offtake deals from Google (200 MW) and Eni.
differentiator: HTS magnets producing fields about four times stronger than existing fusion experiments, allowing a much smaller tokamak.

The goal was to restore US uranium enrichment capacity, where Russia and China dominate HALEU production. Founders Fund incubated the company for about a year, and it was selected for the DOE's HALEU enrichment programme in 2024. It emerged with a $50M Series A in April 2025, with Peter Thiel joining the board.

differentiator: Signed the first commercial fusion power purchase agreement (Microsoft, 2023) and pursues direct electricity recovery rather than steam turbines.

story: Marvel Fusion was founded in Munich in 2019 to pursue non-thermal, laser-driven fusion. Its approach uses precisely controlled short-pulse laser energy to accelerate fuel particles through nanostructured targets, building on the Nobel-winning chirped-pulse amplification work of Strickland and Mourou. The founding team brought nanotechnology, plasma physics, optics and short-pulse laser physics expertise.
product: Inertial (laser) fusion technology using femtosecond lasers and nanostructured targets with hydrogen-boron and mixed fuels.
wedge: Two 100-joule laser prototypes at a demonstration facility built with Colorado State University; initial prototype funding came from SPRIND.
became: Developer of high-energy laser systems and a joint conceptual fusion power plant design with Siemens Energy.
differentiator: Non-thermal, short-pulse laser approach using nanostructured targets, with industrial technology partners (Siemens Energy, TRUMPF, Thales) from early on.

story: newcleo was launched in September 2021 by Stefano Buono, Luciano Cinotti and Elisabeth Rizzotti with a €100M founding round. Its aim is to develop small lead-cooled fast reactors running on MOX fuel made from plutonium and uranium recovered from spent fuel. It raised a further €300M equity round by June 2022 and studied MOX production with Orano. The holding HQ moved from London to Paris in September 2024.

became: Nasdaq-listed advanced reactor developer operating in seven countries, expanding into the US (including a MOX fuel facility partnership with Oklo).
differentiator: Very large early equity raises (€400M within a year of founding) and a combined reactor and fuel-recycling strategy.
